title: Career roadmap · Research Scientist
summary: Build from statistics, programming and computational methods into rigorous interdisciplinary research, with a focus on reproducibility, causal inference, large-scale data and publication-quality scientific work.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. The early years establish mathematical, computational and research-method foundations; the middle years build an identifiable research specialization; later years develop independent research programs, collaborations and scientific leadership.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Develop strong foundations in statistics, machine learning, programming, causal inference, computational social science and reproducible research.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Establish a research identity in an area such as social-network analysis, computational economics, NLP, causal ML, online behaviour, public policy analytics or complex systems.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead multidisciplinary research programs, supervise researchers and connect computational findings to substantive scientific questions.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Lead research agendas using advanced AI, multimodal data, causal methods, large-scale experimentation and responsible data governance.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Keep core statistical and scientific reasoning stronger than any individual software framework. Research scientists who can evaluate causal claims, quantify uncertainty, design credible studies and explain limitations will remain useful even as AI tools and modelling architectures change.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → Research Scientist → Senior Research Scientist → Principal Research Scientist → Research Lead → Associate Research Director → Research Director → Distinguished/Chief Research Scientist

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

A senior research scientist should remain capable of framing original questions, selecting credible methods and judging whether an apparent result is actually meaningful. The role increasingly combines advanced AI with causal inference, multimodal data, large-scale experimentation, research software and responsible data governance. Scientific leadership should remain grounded in reproducibility and uncertainty rather than model complexity alone.
